# N11 current native source port

Source preparation only. The narrow retention correction has12 portable data/
real-file tests passing; no .NET, compiler, native procedure, CI action or Git
mutation was executed. Ordinary product qualification remains closed.

## Entry and prerequisites

`adapter.execute(context, *, deadline)` uses the same13-key root context as the
[owner-death bridge](../owner-death/README.md#entry-contract). It adopts the shared
dispatcher's existing root-owned0700 output containing exactly the five root600
plan/source/build/inventory/execution inputs, checks bindings and creates all new
leaves exclusively. It returns one exact case row for **N11 only**.

The full current capture and actual CLI/helper locked-restore/Release-publication
logs/maps are verified with [binding.py](../../binding.py). The genuine peer helper
comes from the current receipt's helpers.peer.image and is retained through
[slot/helpers.py](../slot/helpers.py). Both historical N02 and N03 prerequisites
still execute physically; they receive no duplicate case credit.

The shared [bridge](../n11/bridge.py) stages full actual inputs via the frozen
owner-death copy helpers with source_sealed=False. Source stays0700 directories/
0644-or0755 files; tool/runtime/helpers are0555 directories/0444-or0555 files. The
runtime is an actual compact FDD deployment, never a fake inventory of an SDK.
The original family shell creates its own request/workspace.

The real [OS audit](../os_audit.py) is called on one capped absolute deadline:
Audit(end), initialize_tools(), then build(runtime,tool,False,peer). The original
[runner](../native_process.py), literal dispatch/FIFO EOF joins, native shell and
retention collector preserve original root-unit/process ownership and cleanup.
No old build schema, TRX, source-review Boolean or successful native result is
fabricated. The N02 actor derives from the actual current checkout UID/GID and
is checked against real NSS; the root adapter cannot substitute a protected owner.

## Native behavior and clocks

N11 is the real synchronous factory stall, original failed stop/frame capture and preserved quarantine.

Fixture600/cleanup30 remain unchanged. N11 creates the original240-second request once and selects its owner runtime from that original remaining budget.
The earlier outer absolute deadline remains in force; no native retry or renewed
allowance is introduced. A fixture failure stays failed even if retention succeeds.

## Evidence and reconciliation

`validate_evidence(context,evidence_raw,*,capture_raw)` checks only the bounded
current-source envelope. It establishes no physical fact. The mandatory
`verify_retained_evidence(context,*,deadline)` rereads actual retained leaves,
command metadata and logs and repeats all original readable record predicates
in [records.py](records.py). Run and aggregate must require both exact rows equal;
execute also performs retained reconciliation itself before returning.

N11-evidence.json binds the original USTAR digest and every unchanged
raw member. The actual collector writes control/native.tar; its stdout is only a
terminal marker. The adapter reads the actual bounded archive, validates it without
filesystem extraction, retains it byte-exact as native-private.tar, and retains each
fixed leaf individually. Aggregate rereads both the actual archive and those leaves;
neither the hash nor the record-validator input is reconstructed from member data.
Original8MiB member/32MiB payload bounds remain; the archive has its separate
33,619,968-byte header/padding bound. Raw records are not echoed; no coverage or
counter arithmetic is performed. The N12 adapter imports the fixed N11 bridge
read-only, bound by the complete current capture.

### Retention helpers and pitfalls

The [bridge](bridge.py) exposes internal data/file helpers used by both adapters:

- `save_archive(path,raw,*,deadline)` exclusively creates only native-private.tar
  in the caller-owned0700 output, uses the separate archive bound, and checks
  opened/named file and parent identity through fsync under the original deadline.
  Production prerequisites already require the caller and output to be root0:0.
- `validate_commands(commands)` requires exactly two terminal command records,
  each with exactly one ordinal-stdout.log and one ordinal-stderr.log row. Stream
  byte counts are integers in0..8MiB and SHA values are64 lowercase hex characters.
- `verify_commands(output,commands,*,deadline)` rereads both real command records
  and both streams, even when their recorded length is zero. Missing/duplicate
  stream rows, missing files, changed bytes, symlinks and hardlinks cannot skip a read.
- Private `validate_packet(...,*,archive_raw,deadline)` requires the actual original
  archive bytes, their exact packet digest and matching member projection before
  forwarding those same bytes to the unchanged record predicates.

Use the actual retained callback for reconciliation; the detached envelope checker
alone cannot establish a physical fact. A Python USTAR reserialization can have the
same members and different bytes, so it must never stand in for original custody.
The [portable controls](../../test_n11.py) exercise metadata and ordinary files only;
their success does not qualify a Linux native case or simulate a protected owner.
